title: The Sea Sonnets 2
text:
Sails that yesterday roamed. Still

they can be seen gleaming in gold and silver.

The rolling brigantine, the frigate

in long flights through the distance.


Pleasant vision of my childhoods, pleasant

and deep vision of an illuminated day,

when the youthful crew

radiated in blue and scarlet.


Pictures the sea brings to the shore

where the lily and the palm tree dance

and repainted shells laugh.


Resplendent landscapes of my sea.

Landscapes that offer themselves, with the vigor

of skies pierced through by suns.
editorial_note: The translation keeps the sonnet's luminous maritime imagery while prioritizing sense over English rhyme.

title: Castilian Language
text:
Solid and lordly verb, language
of robust and transparent architecture.
Strange voice of the pure earth,
the earth that gives birth to lineage.


You bore through the centuries with your message,
woven of vigor and refinement,
of great consistency in its texture:
gold, ivory, precious stone, lace.


The ancient richness of your wealth shines
in the old folios of Castile,
which the imperial seal gave prestige.


Sum of eternities, your legacies
offer, threaded through with graces,
the noblest sayings in their style.
editorial_note: The translation treats 'rancidez' as aged richness rather than decay, matching the poem's praise of Castilian.

title: The Word
text:
Word that denies yourself to my effort;

elusive word, more ardent and pure,

yield to the miracle of my ancient dream

and give me your love and your beauty.


I know that you are summary and design.

I know that you are spirit and figure,

and that, if I disdain the god of your metal,

I will never possess your architecture.


Be for me column and also arch.

Be for me the arrow that from the bow

sets out toward the light of the infinite.


Be, through creative dominion, the summit

where, by the thrust of rhyme,

I must enjoy the loftiness of art.
editorial_note: The translation preserves the architectural and metallic metaphors for poetic language.

title: The Sea Sonnets 1
text:
What wind comes riding on a wave

crowned with light, and in my ears

leaves vast kindled messages

from so many islands of cloudscape and frond?


I imagine on round blue water

ships departing, making noise,

and marking, in skies stunned

by solar boiling, sails in a ring.


I imagine, in ruddy noon,

brisk and youthful sailors

in a group of nervous movement.


The islands in a rhythm of palms;

and burning, in raw light, on the shores,

the wind of childhood, the same wind.
editorial_note: The translation keeps the sonnet's repeated imagined sea and the final return of childhood wind.

title: Foam
text:
Of the lightness of dawn;
of the subtle within the fleeting—mist,
vapor or cloud—there remains in the sea a fine,
flowing and tremulous brushstroke.


Of what the sea refines in its expanse
—pearl in gradation, iridescent shell—,
there remains a brilliant halo in the swell.
A halo that culminates in pure irradiation.


The earth gives the petals of the lily
to the sea, and the sea keeps them. The sea encloses
graces, and graces it adds to its graces.


And it goes showing, when the aureole
of beauty girds sea and wave,
the unsayable white of foam.
editorial_note: The translation preserves the painterly sea imagery and the repeated play on 'graces.'
